senses.gloss: f. (= הִכָּרֵת, v. כָּרַת Nif.) excommunication, extermination; (in Talm. law) divine punishment through premature or sudden death, opp. to מיתה בידי אדם capital punishment.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 60b:17">Snh. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>זובח … כ׳ הוא</he> is not slaughtering consecrated animals outside of the Temple punishable with extinction?, opp. <cite ref="S00778"><he>קטלא</he></cite> death by execution.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 28a:10">M. Kat. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>מת בחמשים שנה זו היא מיתת כ׳</he> if one dies at the age of fifty, that is death of divine visitation; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 2:1:3">Y. Bicc. II, beg. 64ᶜ</cite> <he>בהִיכָּרֵת</he>; <cite ref="Tractate Semachot 3:8">Treat. S’maḥ. III, 8</cite> <he>בהִכָּרֵת</he>.

Ib. 10 וכי מה מודיענו שמיתתם בהכרת what is there to indicate that they died by divine visitation?; Y. l. c. 64ᵈ top שהוא בהיכרת.—M. Kat. l. c. נפקי לי מכ׳ I have escaped the punishment of kareth (being sixty years old). Ib. כ׳ דשני the kareth of years, premature death; כ׳ דיומי the k. of days, sudden death.
Ḥull. 31ᵃ עון כ׳ a transgression punishable with k., opp. איסור מיתה.

Macc. III, 15 (23ᵃ) נפטרו מידי כְּרֵיתָן Ms. M. (ed. ידי כְּרִיתָתָם) are released from k. (which would otherwise await them). Ib. 13ᵇ ולמה יצאת כ׳ באחותו why is the punishment of k. specifically mentioned with reference to incest with a sister (Lev. XX, 17, being included in Lev. XVIII, 29)?—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 28:5">Gen. R. s. 28</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="K01288"><he>כְּרֵתִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="Zephaniah 2:5">Zeph. II, 5</cite>, v. Targ. a. l.) <he>גוי שהוא ראוי כ׳</he> a nation deserving extermination; (Yalk. Zeph. 567 <he>ראוי לִיכָּרֵת</he>); a. v. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="K01182"><he>כְּרִיתוֹת</he></cite> (fr. <cite ref="K01181"><he>כְּרִיתָה</he></cite>).
Ker. I, 1 שלשים ושש כ׳ בתורה there are thirty six transgressions mentioned in the Torah as (eventually) punishable with kareth.
Macc. III, 15, a. fr. חייבי כ׳ those on whose transgressions the penalty of k. is pronounced; a. fr.—K’rithoth, a treatise of the Mishnah, Tosefta, and Talmud Babli, of the Order of Kodashim.
